name: validate_ai_output
description: The merge gate for AI-written CODE: returns a binary approve/reject verdict with veto power â€” e.g. it rejects code calling the nonexistent stripe.Inventory API, or an N+1 loop with the latency arithmetic to prove it. Deterministic reality gates (mock/placeholder veto, gaming and bypass detection, invented-API checks) run first and cannot be overridden; a frontier-model review (ISO/IEC 25010) then scores performance, scalability, reliability and tech debt. Read-only: the code is analyzed, never executed. Call it on every AI-generated diff before accepting it; use validate_plan for plans, analyze_code for an advisory report without a verdict.

arguments.name: ai_output
arguments.desc: The AI-generated code to gate â€” a diff, function or whole file. Plain source text, any mainstream language.

arguments.name: validation_type
arguments.desc: 'code_generation' (default) for source code; 'text' for prose output such as documentation or commit messages.

arguments.name: context
arguments.desc: Optional review context, e.g. {"language": "cpp", "scale": "10k req/s"}. 'language' sharpens SDK-reality checks.

name: validate_plan
description: The gate for PLANS, designs and specs â€” run BEFORE any code is written, the cheapest place to catch a bad design. Returns the same binary verdict shape as validate_ai_output, with findings on completeness, feasibility, performance and scalability implications, security risks and missing considerations (e.g. it rejects a plan that polls an API every 100ms per client, with the request-volume math). Read-only: nothing is executed or stored beyond the verdict. Use validate_ai_output for the code that follows.

arguments.name: plan
arguments.desc: The implementation plan, design or spec to validate, as plain text or markdown â€” e.g. a numbered migration plan or an architecture sketch.

arguments.name: context
arguments.desc: Optional constraints the review should weigh, e.g. {"system": "payments API", "scale": "1M users", "constraints": "PostgreSQL only"}.

name: analyze_code
description: Advisory deep-dive on existing code â€” scores and findings, deliberately NO pass/fail verdict, so it never blocks an agent. Surfaces performance hot paths, scalability cliffs, reliability gaps and tech debt with concrete latency/throughput arithmetic (e.g. 'O(nÂ²) dedup: ~4s at 10k items'). Read-only: the code is analyzed, never executed. Use it to understand a validate_ai_output rejection or review inherited code; use validate_ai_output when you need an accept/reject decision.

arguments.name: code
arguments.desc: The source code to analyze â€” a function, file or pasted excerpt.

arguments.name: analysis_type
arguments.desc: Lens for the review: 'quality' (default, broad ISO/IEC 25010 pass) or a focused pass on one dimension.

arguments.name: language
arguments.desc: Source language, e.g. 'python', 'typescript', 'cpp', 'sql', 'swift'. Inferred if omitted; stating it sharpens findings.

name: generate_code
description: Generate code and gate it in one step: an LLM writes the implementation, then the same protection engine as validate_ai_output vets it â€” retrying generation when the gate rejects. If every attempt is vetoed you still receive the last attempt, clearly marked validated:false with the gate findings â€” rejected code is never presented as clean. Generation runs on our infrastructure; nothing executes in your environment.

arguments.name: prompt
arguments.desc: What to build, with any constraints worth enforcing â€” e.g. 'a rate-limited retry decorator with exponential backoff, stdlib only'.

arguments.name: language
arguments.desc: Target language for the generated code, e.g. 'python' (default), 'typescript', 'go', 'sql'.

arguments.name: max_tokens
arguments.desc: Generation budget. The default 4000 fits most functions/classes; raise it for multi-file scaffolds.
